Main.sentence: Dwight David " Ike " Eisenhower [a] (born David Dwight Eisenhower ; October 14, 1890 – March 28, 1969) was the 34th ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ , serving from 1953 to 1961. During ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ , he was ___E:Supreme Commander of the Allied Expeditionary Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Headquarters_Allied_Expeditionary_Force)___ in Europe and achieved the ___E:five-star rank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five-star_rank)___ as ___E:General of the Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_of_the_Army_(United_States))___ .

Eisenhower planned and supervised two of the most consequential military campaigns of ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_the_United_States_during_World_War_II)___ : ___E:Operation Torch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Torch)___ in the ___E:North Africa campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Africa_campaign)___ in 1942–1943 and the ___E:invasion of Normandy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Normandy)___ in 1944.
Eisenhower was born in ___E:Denison, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denison,_Texas)___ , and raised in ___E:Abilene, Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abilene,_Kansas)___ .
His family had a strong religious background, and his mother became a ___E:Jehovah's Witness U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jehovah%27s_Witness)___ .

Eisenhower, however, belonged to no organized church until 1952. He graduated from ___E:West Point U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Point)___ in 1915 and later married ___E:Mamie Doud U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mamie_Eisenhower)___ , with whom he had two sons. During ___E:World War I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I)___ , he was denied a request to serve in Europe and instead commanded a unit that trained ___E:tank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tank)___ crews.

Between the wars he served in staff positions in the US and the Philippines, reaching the rank of ___E:brigadier general U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigadier_general_(United_States))___ shortly before the entry of the US into World War II in 1941. After further promotion Eisenhower oversaw the Allied invasions of North Africa and ___E:Sicily U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied_invasion_of_Sicily)___ before supervising the invasions of ___E:France U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Overlord)___ and ___E:Germany U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Allied_invasion_of_Germany)___ .

After the war ended in Europe, he served as ___E:military governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_governor)___ of the ___E:American-occupied zone of Germany U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American-occupied_zone_of_Germany)___ (1945), ___E:Army Chief of Staff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_Staff_of_the_United_States_Army)___ (1945–1948), ___E:president of Columbia University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Columbia_University)___ (1948–1953), and as the first ___E:supreme commander of NATO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Allied_Commander_Europe)___ (1951–1952).

In 1952, Eisenhower entered the presidential race as a ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ to block the isolationist foreign policies of Senator ___E:Robert A. Taft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_A._Taft)___ , who opposed ___E:NATO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO)___ .

Eisenhower won ___E:that year's election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_United_States_presidential_election)___ and the ___E:1956 election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_United_States_presidential_election)___ in ___E:landslides U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landslide_victory)___ , both times defeating ___E:Adlai Stevenson II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adlai_Stevenson_II)___ .

Eisenhower's main goals in office were to ___E:contain the spread of communism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Containment)___ and reduce ___E:federal deficits U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_deficit)___ .

In 1953, he considered using ___E:nuclear weapons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_weapon)___ to end the ___E:Korean War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War)___ and may have threatened China with ___E:nuclear attack U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_attack)___ if an armistice was not reached quickly.
China did agree and ___E:an armistice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_Armistice_Agreement)___ resulted, which remains in effect.
His ___E:New Look policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Look_policy)___ of nuclear deterrence prioritized "inexpensive" nuclear weapons while reducing funding for expensive Army divisions.

He continued ___E:Harry S. Truman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman)___ 's policy of recognizing ___E:Taiwan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan)___ as the legitimate government of China, and he won congressional approval of the ___E:Formosa Resolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formosa_Resolution)___ .
His administration provided aid to help the French try to fight Vietnamese Communists in the ___E:First Indochina War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Indochina_War)___ .
After the French left, he gave strong financial support to the new state of ___E:South Vietnam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Vietnam)___ .

He supported ___E:regime-changing military coups U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_involvement_in_regime_change)___ in ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Iranian_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat)___ and ___E:Guatemala U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Guatemalan_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat)___ orchestrated by his own administration.
During the ___E:Suez Crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suez_Crisis)___ of 1956, he condemned the Israeli, British, and French invasion of Egypt, and he forced them to withdraw.
He also condemned the Soviet invasion during the ___E:Hungarian Revolution of 1956 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Revolution_of_1956)___ but took no action.
He deployed 15,000 soldiers during the ___E:1958 Lebanon crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_Lebanon_crisis)___ .

Near the end of his term, a summit meeting with the Soviet leader ___E:Nikita Khrushchev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev)___ was cancelled when ___E:a US spy plane was shot down U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_U-2_incident)___ over the Soviet Union.

Eisenhower approved the ___E:Bay of Pigs Invasion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Pigs_Invasion)___ , which was left to ___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ to carry out.

On the domestic front, Eisenhower governed as a ___E:moderate conservative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moderate_conservative)___ who continued ___E:New Deal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal)___ agencies and expanded ___E:Social Security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Security_(United_States))___ .

He covertly opposed ___E:Joseph McCarthy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_McCarthy)___ and contributed to the end of ___E:McCarthyism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCarthyism)___ by openly invoking ___E:executive privilege U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_privilege)___ .

He signed the ___E:Civil Rights Act of 1957 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Act_of_1957)___ and sent Army troops to enforce federal court orders which ___E:integrated schools in Little Rock, Arkansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Rock_Nine)___ .

His administration undertook the development and construction of the ___E:Interstate Highway System U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_Highway_System)___ , which remains the largest construction of roadways in American history.

In 1957, following the Soviet launch of ___E:Sputnik U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sputnik)___ , Eisenhower led the American response which included the ___E:creation of NASA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creation_of_NASA)___ and the establishment of a stronger, science-based education via the ___E:National Defense Education Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Defense_Education_Act)___ .

The Soviet Union began to reinforce ___E:their own space program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_space_program)___ , escalating the ___E:Space Race U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Race)___ .

His two terms saw ___E:unprecedented economic prosperity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post%E2%80%93World_War_II_economic_expansion)___ except for a ___E:minor recession in 1958 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recession_of_1958)___ .

In ___E:his farewell address U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eisenhower%27s_farewell_address)___ , he expressed his concerns about the dangers of massive ___E:military spending U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_budget_of_the_United_States)___ , particularly ___E:deficit spending U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deficit_spending)___ and government contracts to private military manufacturers, which he dubbed "the ___E:military–industrial complex U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military%E2%80%93industrial_complex)___ ".

Historical evaluations of ___E:his presidency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Dwight_D._Eisenhower)___ place him among the ___E:upper tier of US presidents U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_presidents_of_the_United_States#Scholar_survey_summary)___ .

The Eisenhauer (German for "iron hewer" or "iron miner") family migrated from the German village of ___E:Karlsbrunn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karlsbrunn)___ to the ___E:Province of Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Pennsylvania)___ in 1741.  Accounts vary as to how and when the German name Eisenhauer was ___E:anglicized U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglicisation_(linguistics))___ .

David Jacob Eisenhower, Eisenhower's father, was a college-educated engineer, despite his own father's urging to stay on the family farm. Eisenhower's mother, ___E:Ida Elizabeth (Stover) Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ida_Stover_Eisenhower)___ , of predominantly German Protestant ancestry, moved to Kansas from Virginia.

She married David on September 23, 1885, in ___E:Lecompton, Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lecompton,_Kansas)___ , on the campus of their alma mater, ___E:Lane University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lane_University)___ .
David owned a general store in ___E:Hope, Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope,_Kansas)___ , but the business failed due to economic conditions and the family became impoverished.
The Eisenhowers lived in Texas from 1889 until 1892, and later returned to Kansas, with $24 (equivalent to $840 in 2024) to their name. David worked as a railroad mechanic and then at a creamery.
By 1898, the parents made a decent living and provided a suitable home for their large family.
Eisenhower was born David Dwight Eisenhower in ___E:Denison, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denison,_Texas)___ , on October 14, 1890, the third of seven sons born to Ida and David.
His mother soon reversed his two forenames after his birth to avoid the confusion of having two Davids in the family.
He was named Dwight after the evangelist ___E:Dwight L. Moody U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_L._Moody)___ .

All of the boys were nicknamed "Ike", such as "Big Ike" ( ___E:Edgar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_N._Eisenhower)___ ) and "Little Ike" (Dwight); the nickname was intended as an abbreviation of their last name.  By World War II, only Dwight was still called "Ike".
In 1892, the family moved to ___E:Abilene, Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abilene,_Kansas)___ , which Eisenhower considered his hometown.

As a child, he was involved in an accident that cost his younger brother ___E:Earl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_D._Eisenhower)___ an eye, for which he was remorseful for the remainder of his life.  Eisenhower developed a keen and enduring interest in exploring the outdoors.
He learned about hunting and fishing, cooking, and card playing from a man named Bob Davis who camped on the ___E:Smoky Hill River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoky_Hill_River)___ .
While his mother was against war, it was her collection of history books that first sparked Eisenhower's interest in military history; he became a voracious reader on the subject.
Other favorite subjects early in his education were arithmetic and spelling.
Eisenhower's parents set aside specific times at breakfast and at dinner for daily family Bible reading.
Chores were regularly assigned and rotated among all the children, and misbehavior was met with unequivocal discipline, usually from David.

His mother, previously a member (with David) of the ___E:River Brethren U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Brethren)___ ( ___E:Brethren in Christ Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brethren_in_Christ_Church)___ ) sect of the ___E:Mennonites U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mennonite)___ ,  joined the ___E:International Bible Students Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Bible_Students)___ , later known as ___E:Jehovah's Witnesses U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jehovah%27s_Witnesses)___ .
The Eisenhower home served as the local meeting hall from 1896 to 1915, though Dwight never joined.
His later decision to attend West Point saddened his mother, who felt that warfare was "rather wicked", but she did not overrule his decision.
Speaking of himself in 1948, Eisenhower said he was "one of the most deeply religious men I know" though unattached to any "sect or organization".
He was baptized in the ___E:Presbyterian Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presbyterian_Church_in_the_United_States_of_America)___ in 1953.

Eisenhower attended ___E:Abilene High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abilene_High_School_(Kansas))___ and graduated in 1909.  As a freshman, he injured his knee and developed a leg infection that extended into his groin, which his doctor diagnosed as life-threatening.

The doctor insisted that the leg be amputated but Dwight refused to allow it, and surprisingly recovered, though he had to repeat his freshman year.  He and brother ___E:Edgar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_N._Eisenhower)___ both wanted to attend college, though they lacked the funds.
They made a pact to take alternate years at college while the other worked to earn the tuitions.
Edgar took the first turn at school, and Dwight was employed as a night supervisor at the Belle Springs Creamery.
When Edgar asked for a second year, Dwight consented.

At that time a friend, ___E:Edward "Swede" Hazlett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Hazlett)___ , was applying to the ___E:Naval Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Naval_Academy)___ and urged Dwight to apply, since no tuition was required.
Eisenhower requested consideration for either Annapolis or West Point with his Senator, ___E:Joseph L. Bristow U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_L._Bristow)___ .
Though Eisenhower was among the winners of the entrance-exam competition, he was beyond the age limit for the Naval Academy.
He accepted an appointment to West Point in 1911.
At West Point, Eisenhower relished the emphasis on traditions and on sports, but was less enthusiastic about the hazing, though he willingly accepted it as a plebe.
He was also a regular violator of the more detailed regulations and finished school with a less than stellar discipline rating.
Academically, Eisenhower's best subject by far was English.
Otherwise, his performance was average, though he thoroughly enjoyed the typical emphasis of engineering on science and mathematics.
In athletics, Eisenhower later said that "not making the baseball team at West Point was one of the greatest disappointments of my life, maybe my greatest".

He made the ___E:varsity football team U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_Black_Knights_football)___   and was a starter at ___E:halfback U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halfback_(American_football))___ in 1912, when he tried to tackle the legendary ___E:Jim Thorpe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Thorpe)___ of the ___E:Carlisle Indians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlisle_Indians_football)___ .

Eisenhower suffered a torn knee while being tackled in the next game, which was the last he played; he reinjured his knee on horseback and in the boxing ring,    so he turned to fencing and gymnastics.
Eisenhower later served as junior varsity football coach and cheerleader, which caught the attention of General ___E:Frederick Funston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Funston)___ .

He graduated from West Point in the middle of the class of 1915,  which became known as " ___E:the class the stars fell on U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_class_the_stars_fell_on)___ ", because 59 members eventually became ___E:general officers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_officer)___ .

After graduation in 1915, Second Lieutenant Eisenhower requested an assignment in the Philippines, which was denied; because of the ongoing ___E:Mexican Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Revolution)___ , he was posted to ___E:Fort Sam Houston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Sam_Houston)___ in ___E:San Antonio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio)___ , Texas, under the command of General Funston.

In 1916, while stationed at Fort Sam Houston, Funston convinced him to become the football coach for ___E:Peacock Military Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Military_Academy)___ ;  he later became the coach at St. Louis College, now ___E:St. Mary's University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Mary%27s_University,_Texas)___ ,  and was an honorary member of the Sigma Beta Chi fraternity there.
While Eisenhower was stationed in Texas, he met Mamie Doud of ___E:Boone, Iowa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boone,_Iowa)___ .
They were immediately taken with each other.

He proposed to her on ___E:Valentine's Day U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentine%27s_Day)___ in 1916.  A November wedding date in ___E:Denver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver)___ , Colorado, was moved up to July 1 due to the impending ___E:American entry into World War I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_entry_into_World_War_I)___ ; Funston approved 10 days of leave for their wedding.
The Eisenhowers moved many times during their first 35 years of marriage.

The Eisenhowers had two sons. In late 1917 while he was in charge of training at ___E:Fort Oglethorpe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Oglethorpe,_Georgia)___ in ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state))___ , his wife Mamie had their first son, ___E:Doud Dwight "Icky" Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_of_Dwight_D._Eisenhower#Doud_Eisenhower)___ , who died of ___E:scarlet fever U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarlet_fever)___ at the age of three.
Eisenhower was mostly reluctant to discuss his death.
Their second son, ___E:John Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Eisenhower)___ , was born in 1922 in Denver.

Eisenhower was a golf enthusiast later in life, and he joined the ___E:Augusta National Golf Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augusta_National_Golf_Club)___ in 1948.  He played golf frequently during and after his presidency and was unreserved in his passion for the game, to the point of golfing during winter; he ordered his golf balls painted black so he could see them better against snow. He had a basic golf facility installed at Camp David, and he became close friends with the Augusta National Chairman ___E:Clifford Roberts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clifford_Roberts)___ , inviting Roberts to stay at the ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ on numerous occasions.
Roberts, an investment broker, also handled the Eisenhower family's investments.

He began ___E:oil painting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_painting)___ while at Columbia University, after watching ___E:Thomas E. Stephens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_E._Stephens_(artist))___ paint Mamie's portrait.

Eisenhower painted about 260 oils during the last 20 years of his life. The images were mostly landscapes but also portraits of subjects such as Mamie, their grandchildren, Field Marshal ___E:Bernard Montgomery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Montgomery)___ , ___E:George Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington)___ , and ___E:Abraham Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln)___ .  ___E:Wendy Beckett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Beckett)___ stated that Eisenhower's paintings, "simple and earnest", caused her to "wonder at the hidden depths of this reticent president".

A conservative in both art and politics, Eisenhower in a 1962 speech denounced modern art as "a piece of canvas that looks like a broken-down ___E:Tin Lizzie U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tin_Lizzie)___ , loaded with paint, has been driven over it".
Angels in the Outfield was Eisenhower's favorite movie.
His favorite reading material for relaxation were the Western novels of ___E:Zane Grey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zane_Grey)___ .
With his excellent memory and ability to focus, Eisenhower was skilled at cards.
He learned poker, which he called his "favorite indoor sport", in Abilene.

Eisenhower recorded West Point classmates' poker losses for payment after graduation and later stopped playing because his opponents resented having to pay him. A friend reported that after learning to play ___E:contract bridge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contract_bridge)___ at West Point, Eisenhower played the game six nights a week for five months.
Eisenhower continued to play bridge throughout his military career.
While stationed in the Philippines, he played regularly with President ___E:Manuel Quezon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Quezon)___ , earning him the nickname the "Bridge Wizard of Manila".
An unwritten qualification for an officer's appointment to Eisenhower's staff during World War II was the ability to play bridge.
He played even during the stressful weeks leading up to the D-Day landings.

His favorite partner was General ___E:Alfred Gruenther U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Gruenther)___ , considered the best player in the US Army; he appointed Gruenther his second-in-command at NATO partly because of his skill at bridge.
Saturday night bridge games at the White House were a feature of his presidency.
He was a strong player, though not an expert by modern standards.

The great bridge player and popularizer ___E:Ely Culbertson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ely_Culbertson)___ described his game as classic and sound with "flashes of brilliance" and said that "you can always judge a man's character by the way he plays cards.
Eisenhower is a calm and collected player and never whines at his losses.

He is brilliant in victory but never commits the bridge player's worst crime of gloating when he wins." Bridge expert ___E:Oswald Jacoby U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswald_Jacoby)___ frequently participated in the White House games and said, "The President plays better bridge than golf. He tries to break 90 at golf. At bridge, you would say he plays in the 70s."

Eisenhower served initially in logistics and then the ___E:infantry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infantry)___ at various camps in Texas and ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state))___ until 1918. When the US entered ___E:World War I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I)___ , he immediately requested an overseas assignment but was denied and assigned to ___E:Ft. Leavenworth, Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ft._Leavenworth)___ .

In February 1918, he was transferred to ___E:Camp Meade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_George_G._Meade)___ in ___E:Maryland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland)___ with the ___E:65th Engineers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/65th_Brigade_Engineer_Battalion)___ .

Historian ___E:John Lewis Gaddis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lewis_Gaddis)___ has summarized a more recent turnaround in evaluations by historians:
Historians long ago abandoned the view that Eisenhower's was a failed presidency.
He did, after all, end the Korean War without getting into any others.
He stabilized, and did not escalate, the Soviet–American rivalry.
He strengthened European alliances while withdrawing support from European colonialism.
He rescued the Republican Party from isolationism and McCarthyism.

He maintained prosperity, balanced the budget, promoted technological innovation, facilitated (if reluctantly) the civil rights movement and warned, in the most memorable farewell address since Washington's, of a "military–industrial complex" that could endanger the nation's liberties.
Not until Reagan would another president leave office with so strong a sense of having accomplished what he set out to do.
